design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 0 of driver_account_holds_and_deactivations (Wayfare Mobility, category driver). Round 2 (rework after the policy-task audit); every figure below is the output of the verification run recorded at the end.

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0: prerequisite_problems 2, problems 3, factor_counts [6, 6, 6]. Root plus two prerequisite problems, six factors each. Claimed: driver_ext_document_lapse_allowance (deactivation for document lapse dated by the lapse allowance, tool deactivate_for_document_lapse_e185dacd), driver_ext_insurance_binder_acceptance (insurance binder accepted period, tool record_insurance_binder_0f7a5736), driver_ext_temporary_license_acceptance (paper temporary license accepted period, user tool upload_temporary_license_ef094b46). Task 1 claims the other four policies (warning sequence, registration hold start, inspection validity, temporary permit); scopes are disjoint and cover all seven.

[Why this is a good test] Lucia asks one plain thing — put her paper temporary license on file. The 21 accepted days cannot be produced without (a) reading, in the temporary-license rule, that its figure waits on the insurance expiry date carrying every uploaded binder and on the agreement showing any deactivation a document hold has run into; (b) working out that her July hold has outrun its lapse allowance — 76 days, because both insurance expiry notices were sent, so the lapse clock runs from the second notice (2026-06-24), not from the hold start — so the deactivation is owed, dated 2026-09-16; (c) recording the pending binder for 32 days, whose takeover clock counts the binder's cover from its upload date (the insurance had lapsed before it was uploaded) and whose standing adjustment changes once the deactivation lands; and only then (d) the license figure, whose takeover clock counts from the old card's expiry (2026-10-16). Depth: three writes in forced order. Breadth: standing record (notices, uploads, reviews, warnings), agreement dates, the earnings account (cross-category) and earlier writes of the same call. Each problem has exactly one tool, so the difficulty is in the policy and the records.

[Problem-tree card] Root driver_ext_temporary_license_acceptance (on_request, user tool upload_temporary_license_ef094b46). Edges (state form, value_input):
 E1 driver_ext_temporary_license_acceptance -> driver_ext_insurance_binder_acceptance: gate short_doc_adj; sentence (negated): "The temporary license acceptance days are not worked out until the auto insurance expiry date on the agreement carries the accepted period of every insurance binder uploaded to the standing record."; false at opening: insurance_expiry_date 2026-07-01 while the binder upload 5214629c-eaab-4dc9-b843-a061842198a4 (2026-10-06, printed end 2026-12-07) is on the standing record; resolved by record_insurance_binder_0f7a5736 (agent), the only write that sets the insurance expiry date from a binder. Derivation: sentence + records + the binder rule ('A binder updates the agreement only when support records it') -> record the binder.
 E2 driver_ext_temporary_license_acceptance -> driver_ext_document_lapse_allowance: gate standing_adj; sentence (affirmative 'Before ... must'): "Before the temporary license acceptance days are worked out, the agreement's status must already show the deactivation for document lapse owed by any document hold that has run past its lapse allowance."; false at opening: status on_hold, hold_started_date 2026-07-02, deactivation_reason none, while the 76-day allowance ran out 2026-09-16; resolved by deactivate_for_document_lapse_e185dacd (agent), the only write giving a document-lapse deactivation. Derivation: sentence + records + the lapse rule ('A document hold still in place on the day its lapse allowance days run out ends in deactivation for document lapse') -> compute the allowance, find it run out, deactivate.
 E3 driver_ext_insurance_binder_acceptance -> driver_ext_document_lapse_allowance: gate standing_adj; sentence (affirmative 'only after'): "The binder acceptance days are fixed only after the agreement's status and deactivation date already show any deactivation for document lapse that its document hold has run into."; same opening facts and resolving write as E2.
 Directions: E1 negated, E2/E3 affirmative. Topological order driver_ext_document_lapse_allowance -> driver_ext_insurance_binder_acceptance -> driver_ext_temporary_license_acceptance (unique). Deletion runs: skip binder -> license 15 (not 21); skip deactivation -> binder 35 (not 32), license 25 (not 21). user_scenario names no prerequisite; no tool validates one.

[Base-invariant card] driver_ext_document_lapse_allowance subject driver_deactivate: governing base policies driver_rating_standard, driver_cancellation_standard, driver_document_compliance, driver_background_recheck_rules, driver_safety_rules, driver_voluntary_close_rules — no gate applies to driver_deactivate, all policy scope; overwrite on driver_document_compliance's 'A document hold still in place document_hold_max_days after hold_started_date ends in deactivation for document_lapse'; the reversal clause stays inherited and does not fire (the inspection stays lapsed). driver_ext_insurance_binder_acceptance subject driver_document_update: driver_document_compliance policy scope; overwrite of the upload sentence for binders. driver_ext_temporary_license_acceptance subjects driver_document_submit + driver_document_update: driver_document_compliance gate not_closed (status on_hold at opening, deactivated after step 6, never closed; agreement id = call argument). No time gate applies.

[Business-object card] One agreement 49e953a0-3f65-4c84-ad3e-3d9eddcb8b19. Binder = latest auto_insurance upload 5214629c-eaab-4dc9-b843-a061842198a4. Lapsed document = earliest expiry among license 2026-10-16, insurance 2026-07-01, inspection 2026-09-15 and the registration on file 2027-03-31 = the auto insurance. Notices covering 2026-07-01: 06c10078-38e4-4f80-8a5f-098c8570af31 (2026-06-01) and f95bcdd2-9c7c-4a52-8315-81b26f8db0ae (2026-06-24); notices of the 2024 and 2025 insurance terms cover other dates and are excluded (near miss for the lapse clock). Second notices inside 24 months: 2025-06-24, 2026-06-24, 2026-09-08, 2026-10-09; outside: 2024-06-24 at 27 months (near miss — counting it would move the license late-renewal tier from 'three or four' to 'five or more', 21 -> 17, and the binder late-renewal tier from 'exactly two' to 'three or more', 32 -> 28). Warnings: 2026-05-11 inside 6 months, 2025-11-03 outside (near miss for the lapse allowance, 76 -> 71).

[Factor cards — each method factor's three tiers compute three different formula shapes (round 3: the license takeover's second tier now takes off the uncovered days beyond 14, at most 10, instead of repeating the first tier's expression)]
 driver_ext_document_lapse_allowance (opening world): tenure 2678 days +10 (baseline gives 66); Pro Silver (earnings, cross-difficulty) +5 (71); insurance lapsed -20 (96); latest review 4.88 +4 (72); one recent warning -5 (81); lapse clock (method) from the second notice's date, -8 days (84). Fall-back 90. Gold 76.
 driver_ext_insurance_binder_acceptance (after step 6): lapse 102 days -10 (42); exactly two late insurance notices -6 (38); Pro Silver AND tenure >= 1095 (multi-source, cross-difficulty) +4 (28); 62-day term +10 (22); deactivated -6 (38); takeover clock (method) from the upload date, -5 (37). Fall-back 45. Gold 32.
 driver_ext_temporary_license_acceptance (after steps 6 and 8): license takeover (method) from the old card's expiry, +5 (16); check 243 days back +3 (18); one short document -6 (27); four late notices -6 (27); Pro Silver +3 (18); deactivated -8 (29). Fall-back 30. Gold 21.
 Each tier rests on dated rows or agreement dates, never on a stamp; every ladder is stated in full in its rule.

[Seed rows and why] customers (identity); driver_agreements (all dates the factors read; the hold that drives the deactivation); earnings_accounts (Wayfare Pro Silver for Q4 2026: Q2 and Q3 Gold, set from Q1/Q2 metrics within Gold's 8.00% and 4.80 gates (2026-01-12 review 7.2% / 4.89, 2026-06-08 review 7.6% / 4.88); Q3 brought no trips while on hold, so the 2026-10-01 evaluation dropped one level, the most status protection allows; balance 0.00 and points 0 with no ledger, consistent with no trips since July); standing record: insurance uploads and notices (both notices for 2026-07-01 — the 2026-06-24 second notice added in round 2), license upload and notices, inspection notices, registration upload, recheck 2026-02-10, five rating reviews and two cancellation warnings (sequence 1 then 2, each the cycle number of its own day under the warning-cycle rule: fresh cycle, then a recount with severity 1 and Pro Gold forgiveness 2). Automatic clauses: the base document hold already in place; the 90-day lapse clause superseded and discharged by step 6; document_lapse reactivation does not fire (inspection still lapsed); no recheck due; no safety reports; deactivation close period runs to 2027-03-15.

[Persona] Unchanged in round 2: Lucia opens with the surface goal only; phone 8015550186 to locate, date of birth 1988-03-14 to verify, email as a fallback; facts only when asked (not driving since early July, binder uploaded 6 October, inspection lapsed in September); passive reactions to a deactivation (one question the base answers: document-lapse deactivations reverse once every required document is on file), to the binder, the handed-over upload with the given values, and close. No extra asks.

[Reachability] Locate -> verify -> read agreement, standing record, earnings account -> unlock+call deactivation -> unlock+call binder -> unlock_user + Lucia's call. Every argument is computed (allowance_days, accepted_days) or copied from a lookup (driver_agreement_id, hold_started_date). One frozen_time; the renewal and the binder upload predate the call.

[Most likely mistakes] the standard 90 days, or a clock from the hold start (84, 2026-09-24); computing the binder before the deactivation (35) or counting its cover from the recording day (37); computing the license on the opening world (15 or 25) or from the upload day (16); counting the 2024-06-24 notice or the 2025-11-03 warning; treating the registration as never lapsing into the lapsed-document choice (it is a candidate, here not the earliest); lifting the hold (the inspection is lapsed).

[Standard solution] 76 -> deactivate dated 2026-09-16; 32 -> insurance on file to 2026-11-12; Lucia uploads with 21 -> license on file to 2026-11-01.

[Revision log — round 2]
 G-1/T0-1 symptom: the lapse allowance's only method factor multiplied the same length by 125/110/100 percent. Root cause: a rate swap labelled method. Change: the expiry-notice factor is now the lapse-clock rule — the clock runs from the second notice's date, the lapsed expiry date or the hold start, a change of the date the quantity is measured from; the seed gains the 2026-06-24 second notice (f95bcdd2-9c7c-4a52-8315-81b26f8db0ae) so the both-notices tier is exercised. Re-run: 93 -> 76, deactivation 2026-10-03 -> 2026-09-16.
 O-1 (rate-and-rounding method factors, mandatory per coordinator): the binder's and temporary license's standing ladders are now honest parameters (-6/-3/0 and -8/-4/0) and each gained a takeover-clock method (cover counted from the old document's expiry, the upload date, or the recording/upload day); the binder dropped its insurance-history factor and the license its old-license ladder to stay at six factors. Re-run: binder 41 -> 32, license 14 -> 21.
 O-4: the vehicle registration on file now competes in the lapsed-document choice. O-7: each standing ladder names its fall-through ('any other standing'). O-T0-a: both notices now on record. O-T0-b: the license late-renewal ladder gained a five-or-more tier, so the 27-month notice is a genuine near miss.
 Propagation: computations, every call's tracing, objectives/necessity of the standing-record read, contract effects and seed checks, closure edges/flips/order/load-bearing, this dossier.

[Revision log — round 3]
 G2-1 / R2-T0-1 symptom: the license takeover's first two tiers computed the same expression (days from the upload day to the old expiry). Change: tier 2 (license expired at least relapse_days before the upload) now counts the cover from the upload day and takes off only the uncovered days beyond relapse_days, at most lapse_cap_days; tier 1 adds the days to the old expiry; tier 3 changes nothing. On a world with the license on file at 2026-09-10 tier 2 gives 6 where the old shared expression gave 1; this world takes tier 1 (+5), so gold 21 and every sensitivity are unchanged. The order sentence was reworded ('adds days to them or takes days off them as it states') so it no longer restates the tier-1 shape.
 O2-T0-a: the binder late-renewal ladder gained a 'three or more' tier (-10); this world takes 'exactly two' (-6, unchanged), and the 27-month notice is now a genuine near miss (32 -> 28).
 O2-1: the lapse clock's second-notice tier now requires a sequence-2 notice among the covering notices (otherwise the expiry-date tier applies); this world is unchanged (76).
 Propagation: the license, binder and lapse factor traces, the binder late-renewal tier label, this dossier.

[Verification] Scratch run (handling-time evaluation with check_compute's own build_env/eval_compute, real tool replay): gold A 76 (baseline 90), B 32 (baseline 45), C 21 (baseline 30); skip A: B 35, C 25; skip B: C 15. Gate record in the final report.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the three published rules, the three lookups and Lucia's lines: order forced by the waiting sentences; 76, 32, 21. No value sits on a tier boundary (2678 days, 4.88, 102 days, a 62-day term, 243 days, 32 days of insurance left against the 30-day short threshold, 5 days left on the license).
user_scenario: You are Lucia Serrano, a 38-year-old driver in Salt Lake City who has driven on the Wayfare Comfort agreement since 2019. You are organised but tired of paperwork this year, and you speak plainly and a little wearily. On Friday you renewed your driver's license at the Utah Driver License Division; your old card runs out on October 16 and they gave you a paper temporary license to carry until the new card arrives in the mail. You are calling Wayfare support today to get that temporary license on file so your driver profile does not end up showing an expired license. You open with something like: "Hi, I renewed my driver's license on Friday and all I have right now is the paper temporary one until the card comes in the mail. My old license expires on the 16th, so I want to get the temporary one on file with Wayfare." When the agent asks how to find your account you give your mobile number, 8015550186. Only when the agent asks you to verify who you are do you give your date of birth, 1988-03-14; if they want one more detail you give your email, lucia.serrano@outlook.com. You do not know any reference numbers and you never read out anything else from your profile unless asked for it. If the agent asks whether you are driving at the moment, you say you have not driven since early July. If the agent asks about your car insurance, you say you switched to a new insurer and uploaded the new insurance binder in the app on October 6. If the agent asks about your vehicle inspection, you say you know it ran out in September and you have not had the car re-inspected yet. You are fine with the agent taking care of whatever their rules say has to be handled on your account for this; you do not ask what or why beyond what the agent chooses to explain. If the agent tells you your agreement has been deactivated, you are taken aback ("Deactivated? I didn't realise it had been that long.") and you ask once whether it comes back once all your papers are in; whatever the agent answers, you accept it and carry on. If the agent says your insurance binder is now on your file, you say that's the one you uploaded on the 6th. When the agent hands the temporary license upload over to you and tells you exactly what to enter, you run it yourself with exactly the values the agent gives you, and then read back the expiry date it shows you. If that date is earlier than you hoped, you say your permanent card should arrive before then, so that's fine. Once the agent tells you the temporary license is on file, you thank them and end the call; you do not raise anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.driver_agreement_id: Value 49e953a0-3f65-4c84-ad3e-3d9eddcb8b19. Basis: find_driver_agreements with the verified customer_id returns exactly one agreement for Lucia Serrano, driver_agreement_id 49e953a0-3f65-4c84-ad3e-3d9eddcb8b19; the tool docstring asks for 'the reference number of the driver services agreement ... as returned by the driver agreement lookup'.
